NUTRITION AND PREGNANCY

Many active women have sweet dreams about becoming moms. Others
have nightmares about the effect pregnancy will have on their bodies.
Competitive athletes, in particular, worry about “getting fat.” Remember
that pregnancy and obesity are very different! The 25 to 35 pounds (11
to 16 kg) gained during pregnancy can be accounted for by the weight of
the baby (8 Ib, or 3.6 kg), placenta (2 to 3 Ib, or 0.9 to 1.4 kg), amniotic
fluid (2 to 3 Ib, or 0.9 to 1.4 kg), uterus (2 to 5 Ib, or 0.9 to 2.3 kg), breast
tissue (2 to 3 lb, or 0.9 to 1.4 kg), blood supply (4 Ib, or 1.8 kg), and fat
stores for delivery and breastfeeding (5 to 9 Ib, or 2.3 to 4 kg). The Institute
of Medicine (2009) recommends that women who are underweight at
the start of pregnancy gain more weight (28 to 40 Ib, or 13 to 18 kg) and
